summary: Turn the manager-only vacation feed at /org/{orgId}/requests into every member's inbox and put a real Request entity behind it: a member raises an access or question request against another member, the addressee answers or declines with a reason, and only the requester (or an admin) writes granted. Three new tables (Request, RequestMessage, RequestEvent) and one defaulted column (Organization.nextRequestNumber) carry it; every status write happens inside a transaction that re-read the row with FOR UPDATE, and the number is allocated under a lock on the organization row. The list endpoint composes two sections in one response - spec-01 Request rows and spec-10's unchanged vacation cards - under one status vocabulary, retiring the spec-10 pending/approved/rejected values on this endpoint and making an unknown value a 400. Overdue is derived per reading account's timezone and stored nowhere; nothing in this spec sends mail. READ THIS FIRST: this branch already carries a full implementation of the spec from five earlier runs (commits 481a165, 6f2dbb5, e17de7a, 2d802e9, 37b27c4), and the spec was then corrected by a person in 3d46cb3. Only T1, T2 and T3 are open work; T4 through T10 name the file that already holds each part, so the plan accounts for the whole spec without asking for any of it to be written twice. The three open items are the delta between commit 3d46cb3's corrections and the code, plus the one carried code blocker that is still present.

doubleBehaviours.behaviour: MailService records nothing, because nothing calls it
doubleBehaviours.whyItMatters: TC-01-INT-21 asserts a zero count against a recording double (the overrideProvider pattern at apps/api/test/clients.spec.ts:136) rather than against the spec's prose. Requirement 47 is a claim about this system, not an external one, and the double is what turns it into an observation. There is no third-party system in this spec: its External Contracts row says the feature depends on no external service, no API key and no MCP server, and no credential for it appears in any tracked file - so there is no Assumed external observation carrying a requirement, and no other double to plan.

dsGaps.resolution: Three call sites ship a native <textarea> carrying design-system tokens and no literal of its own: NewRequestModal.tsx (description), DeclineRequestModal.tsx (reason) and the detail screen's message composer. T3 replaces the eight remaining size literals with the tokens that already hold those exact values. What closes the gap is a Textarea in @ds with the same token contract, adopted by all three call sites at once - not this release, and never a per-screen style.

NewRequestModal.tsx ships a native <input type="date"> with the same token treatment; the browser control is the accessible option and needs no polyfill. What closes the gap is a DateField in @ds. Recorded here rather than improvised: the rule is that anything missing goes into the design system, and until it does the gap is written down.

risks.risk: The plan is mostly a verification of work already on the branch, so an implementer could read T4-T10 as an instruction to rewrite them and produce a large diff that later stages must review from scratch.
risks.mitigation: Every one of those tasks opens with `PRESENT at HEAD` and names the file and line that already holds the work. Only T1, T2 and T3 are marked OPEN. The diff this run should produce is a handful of lines in four files plus one E2E case.

risks.risk: T1's fix is invisible today: with only view-all-requests read on that screen, the normalized and un-normalized answers coincide for every role the database currently holds.
risks.mitigation: That is precisely why it is a blocker rather than a nicety - the next capability added to the screen inherits a silent false. The fix is one line and matches the two sibling files, so a reviewer can check it by diffing three call sites.

risks.risk: T3 touches styling in four files and could tempt a repo-wide sweep of the ten other `1.5px solid` literals in apps/web.
risks.mitigation: T3's scope is fixed to the four files this spec adds. The precedent file the spec names, apps/web/app/org/[orgId]/members/[memberId]/RejectRequestModal.tsx:198, carries the same literal and belongs to spec 09; touching it would put another spec's screen in this diff.
